svg.title: Four Gates Before a Land Offer
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-comping-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Gates Before a Land Offer; subtitle: Sold comps, site layers, disclosure status, and the max-buy cap; caption: Operators value vacant land off sold, land-only comps, pull wetland and flood layers, haircut list prices in non-disclosure states, and walk when the number will not clear the cap.; assumptions note: Gate order consolidates the comping practices of the cited practitioners; discount bands and caps are their reported rules of thumb, not appraisal standards.; note: Attributed to Seth Williams of REtipster (rYCHQ59jzhY), Alex Reese of Acrewell Land Company (TbH_4hSsYHU), Sumner Advanced (8pB5HoHJ4Bk), Cool Wholesaling (3x8J7AdyCEw), Brent Bowers, and the Apke Brothers (bIqgihxHoo8).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Are the comps sold, land-only, in a tight size band, and inside a six-to-twelve-month window?; pass next: G2; fail action: Drop actives and outliers that do not line up with the sold list before averaging per-acre values.; gate: G2; question: Have wetlands, flood zone, and soil layers been pulled?; pass next: G3; fail action: Pull them first; a lot about 40 percent wet sold at $20,000 after an $85,000 ask.; gate: G3; question: Is the sold price disclosed in this state?; pass next: G4; fail action: Haircut last list price by days on market (0-15% at 1-90 days, 20-30% at 3-6 months, 35-50% at 6-12 months), drop listings older than a year, and check land.com sold listings.; gate: G4; question: Does the offer clear the max-buy cap (e.g. $35,000 max on 8 Fairmont acres worth $40,000 retail)?; pass next: Send the offer; fail action: Walk away; on subdivides, call the county on minimum lot rules before modeling any split.

text.title: Four Gates Before a Land Offer
text.tspan: Four Gates Before a Land Offer

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Are the comps sold, land-only, in a tight size band, and inside a six-to-twelve-month window?; pass next: G2; fail action: Drop actives and outliers that do not line up with the sold list before averaging per-acre values.
gate: G2; question: Have wetlands, flood zone, and soil layers been pulled?; pass next: G3; fail action: Pull them first; a lot about 40 percent wet sold at $20,000 after an $85,000 ask.

gate: G3; question: Is the sold price disclosed in this state?; pass next: G4; fail action: Haircut last list price by days on market (0-15% at 1-90 days, 20-30% at 3-6 months, 35-50% at 6-12 months), drop listings older than a year, and check land.com sold listings.

gate: G4; question: Does the offer clear the max-buy cap (e.g. $35,000 max on 8 Fairmont acres worth $40,000 retail)?; pass next: Send the offer; fail action: Walk away; on subdivides, call the county on minimum lot rules before modeling any split.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order consolidates the comping practices of the cited practitioners; discount bands and caps are their reported rules of thumb, not appraisal standards.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order consolidates the comping practices of the cited practitioners; discount bands and caps are their reported
rules of thumb, not appraisal standards.
